criteria.justification: The response opens with a clear, unambiguous decision: 'I would order an immediate rollback of the new launch,' with no hedging.

The response treats rollback as straightforward and reversible ('Monitor the dashboards to confirm...drop back to baseline levels') but never explicitly considers or contrasts a fast-fix-forward alternative and its unvalidated risk.

The response explicitly weighs ongoing customer harm ('leaving core functionality broken for existing customers for several days is catastrophic') against the cost of walking back the announcement ('PR embarrassment is temporary; breaking your core product is a fundamental failure of reliability').
The response avoids pushing a rushed fix, instead choosing rollback so Engineering can build the fix properly 'without the pressure of a live, high-severity incident breathing down their necks.'
The response lays out a full follow-up plan including support scripts, a public status update, briefing leadership, and a path back to re-launch once the fix is built.
